extracted.intended_audience: developers/creators submitting Show HN posts on Hacker News
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for authors to prepare and post a 'Show HN' submission on Hacker News so it attracts constructive discussion and avoids being treated as promotion. Covers title, URL usage, content expectations, onboarding, and community etiquette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'Show HN' in the title for demonstrable work
rubrics_metrics.description: If you're sharing your own work and there's a way to try it out, put 'Show HN' in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure you've read the Show HN guidelines: https://news.ycombinator.com/showhn.html.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a URL (posts without URLs get penalized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Posts without URLs get penalized, so when you submit, put your site in the URL field and leave the text field blank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the site in the URL field rather than pasting it into the text body; leaving the text field blank is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add a comment with the backstory
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a comment to the thread giving the backstory of how you came to work on this, and explaining what's different about it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tends to seed discussion in a good direction; use that first comment to provide context beyond the demo itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a clear statement of what the project is/does
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a clear statement of what your project is or does.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't, the discussion will consist of 'I can't tell what this is'. Be explicit and concise about the product's purpose and functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link related prior HN submissions or discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are previous HN submissions or discussions that your work relates to, readers always like to see links to those.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links to earlier posts or relevant threads to help readers place your project in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid marketing/sales language; be factual and direct
rubrics_metrics.description: Drop any language that sounds like marketing or sales. On HN, that is an instant turnoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use factual, direct language. Personal stories and technical details are great. Promotional phrasing is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: the product/project must actually exist and be tryable
rubrics_metrics.description: For Show HN, the product/project needs to actually exist and there needs to be a way for people to try it out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It can't just be a landing page or market test or fundraiser or a blog post or a curated list or other reading material. Please respect this rule; otherwise nearly every post would be a Show HN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make it easy to try without barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Please make it easy for users to try your thing out, preferably without having to sign up, get a confirmation email, and other such barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You'll get more feedback that way, and HN users get ornery if you make them jump through hoops.

rubrics_metrics.name: If hardware or not web-tryable, show how it works via media
rubrics_metrics.description: If it's hardware or something that's not so easy to try out over the internet, find a different way to show how it actually works — a video, for example, or a detailed post with photos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, demonstrative media or documentation so readers can evaluate the project without direct trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a personal (non-brand) username
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't have your username be that of your company or project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It creates a feeling of using the site for promotion and of not really participating as a person. You don't have to use your real name, just something to indicate that you're here as a human, not a brand. If you'd like to change your username, email hn@ycombinator.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optionally provide an email in your profile for contact/repost invites
rubrics_metrics.description: If you're comfortable doing so, put your email address in your profile so we can contact you if we notice anything, and also so we can send you a repost invite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is optional but can facilitate staff contact and repost opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid booster/promotional comments from friends/fans
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your friends and fans do not add booster comments in the thread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HN users are adept at picking up on those and consider it spamming; they will flame you for it. If a friend or a fan has something interesting to say, that's fine, but comments should not be promotional.
